title: Where a value comes from: declared, asked of the program, or free (issue 25: open lists)
note: A list whose members are only known at runtime (issue #25). 2026-11-13: tried, not only read. A program declared with argenv 0.3.2 cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor more positionals than it names: a list needs a closed set of tokens, and only a list repeats. It is one need with three faces - snapall's --only declared as plain text (October, where this issue came from); an id typed from memory and refused three times in ocoeco's form (this week); and ocoeco's own --gathers, move TABLE ID..., and note --set, which cannot be declared at all. The three options in the issue ask how to permit free values; what the week showed is that the question is where values come from: declared (a closed set), asked (known only at runtime, and the program can tell them), or free (anything).
next: the declaration says where an input's values come from; an asked one names nothing but that the program can be asked - so a shell offers them as one types, a form lets one choose, and a list of them is simply declared

title: Completions asked as one types: entering made interactive without a terminal view
note: The author, 2026-11-13: argenv can let completions be regenerated on the fly, making the entering of a command itself interactive. What it stands on is already open here: a list whose members are known only at runtime (argenv-open-lists) - the id of an existing row is such a list. 2026-11-13: it is the same need - a value asked of the program is what a shell can offer as one types.
